Subject: DPA redlines (first pass)

Hi Karthik,

Attached are our first-pass redlines to Redwood's standard DPA — we've highlighted three areas that need negotiation before our legal team can sign: subprocessors (DataHarbor requires prior written approval for new subprocessors), EU->US transfers (we prefer SCCs + specific mapping table and a written transfer impact assessment), and audit rights (we want explicit audit rights beyond SOC reports).

Key asks summarized:
- Prior approval for any new subprocessor that will access personal data; right to object within 14 days.
- Use of EU Standard Contractual Clauses with a completed transfer assessment appended.
- Certification of data deletion/return at contract termination.
- Audit right: on-demand audits at customer expense or reasonable alternative (technical evidence + SOC 2 + right to escalate to onsite auditing for cause).

We also flagged a few liability cap points that our commercial team may discuss separately with your sales rep. Please confirm receipt and confirm who on your side will own the redlines so we can move to a DocuSign exchange when ready.

Thanks,
Susan

Thanks for the loop. I reviewed DataHarbor's redlines; below are privacy counsel notes and a suggested negotiating posture we think is reasonable for a platform like Redwood that offers hosted and private deployments. Please use these points when discussing with DataHarbor's counsel: 

1) Subprocessors
- Redwood position: transparent registry + 30 days' notice of new subprocessors + ability to object for material changes that would increase risk. We should offer a short escalation timeline (14 days) for objections and commit to either stop using the subprocessor for that customer's data or offer mitigation.
- Rationale: prior written approval for every vendor is operationally untenable and will block platform improvements (e.g., monitoring, telemetry, minor infra vendors).

2) Transfers (EU -> US)
- We already apply EU SCCs for EU data flows and maintain a documented transfer impact assessment. Offer to attach the SCCs as an appendix to the DPA and provide the TIA upon request. If DataHarbor insists on a specific mapping table, we can provide a high-level mapping and confirm that SCCs apply.

3) Audit rights
- Offer: quarterly SOC 2 Type II reports + the ability to request supplementary evidence (configuration screenshots, logging summary) + for-cause on-site audits limited to no more than once per 12 months and with reasonable notice, at customer's expense. Unlimited on-site audits are a non-starter.

4) Deletion/return of data
- We will provide certification of deletion upon termination for hosted customers; for on-prem/private deployments, we will provide instructions and support for data removal and a signed attestation where applicable.

5) Breach notification
- Commit to 72 hours initial notification and regular updates; provide SOC/external notifications for incidents affecting multiple customers.

I'll prepare tracked changes to their doc and attach Redwood_proposed_DPA_redlines.docx. Once we have DataHarbor's response to these points, we can decide on DocuSign routing and signature order.

Neha
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — follow up and DataHarbor counterpoints

Neha — thanks for the clear proposal. A few counterpoints from our side: 

- Subprocessors: we cannot accept a pure notice-and-objection model for certain categories (payment processors, analytics where DataHarbor PII may be enriched). For those we need prior written approval. Can Redwood mark these categories in the DPA and commit to prior approval only for them?

- SCCs & TIA: acceptable in principle but DataHarbor needs the full TIA (not just high-level) before final signature. Please provide the most recent TIA and confirm the SCC annex is included in the DocuSign packet.

- Audit rights: SOC2 is acceptable as the baseline. We will require a right to one for-cause on-site audit per 12-month period in addition to SOC2; we will agree to reasonable notice and cost recovery for Redwood.

- Deletion certification: please confirm the exact language you will commit to — DataHarbor needs an attestation that all customer personal data will be deleted from backups within X days of termination (suggest 90 days).

If you can update the DPA with these clarifications, we'll do a quick internal review and aim to route via DocuSign afterwards.

Best,
Susan

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — proposed compromise and next steps

Susan — appreciate the quick turnaround. Below is Redwood's proposed compromise to unblock execution quickly: 

1) Subprocessors — carveout by category: Redwood will provide a subprocessor category table in the DPA. For high-risk categories (payment processors, analytics that process raw PII, customer support tools accessing PII) Redwood will require prior written approval. For all other categories, Redwood will provide 30 days' notice and a 14-day objection window.

2) SCCs & TIA — Redwood will attach SCCs as Appendix A and provide the most recent TIA on request. We will include a statement in the DocuSign packet confirming SCC adoption for EU transfers.

3) Audit rights — Redwood will deliver the latest SOC 2 Type II report and agrees to one for-cause on-site audit per 12 months with reasonable notice (min 30 days) and at customer expense; investigations limited in scope to customer data processing only.

4) Deletion — Redwood to commit to purging customer data from production and application-level backups within 90 days of contract termination and to provide a deletion attestation upon request.

If these items look acceptable, we'll upload the tracked-redline DPA to DocuSign and route the envelope for signature. Proposed routing: Redwood signs first, DataHarbor executes last. If DataHarbor needs a different routing order, please flag now.

I've attached Redwood_proposed_DPA_redlines.docx and included a DocuSign draft link below so your legal ops can preview before we send the live envelope.

DocuSign (preview): https://app.docusign.com/corda/agreements/0a1b2c3d-dataharbor-dpa

Thanks — keen to get this across the line this week.

Karthik
